project.name: How a Thermos Works
project.description: Minimal hand-drawn stick figure explainer about how a vacuum flask keeps drinks hot

source.text: Ever wonder why your coffee goes cold in five minutes but a thermos keeps it hot all day?
Heat escapes a regular mug three ways: conduction, convection, and radiation.
A thermos is basically two bottles, one inside the other, with a vacuum sealed between them.
Conduction needs molecules to bump into each other. A vacuum has no molecules, so heat gets stuck.
The inner wall is mirrored, so heat radiating outward just bounces right back into your drink.
A tight stopper traps convection currents inside, so warm air can't swirl up and out.
The same trick works in reverse, which is why a thermos keeps ice water cold too.
So your thermos isn't magic. It just blocks every escape route heat has.
